title: What do these six subtractions with too few tokens give?
description: Six subtractions are completed with tokens. In each one the tray has too few tokens, so zero pairs are put out before the tokens are lifted off. The tokens that stay give each answer and its sign.
teaching_notes: One idea: put out as many zero pairs as the tokens that are missing, then lift off the tokens being subtracted. Watch for students who work out the smaller number minus the larger and lose the sign.

video_script.why: The child completes six subtractions where the tray has too few tokens, by putting out zero pairs first.
video_script.substitution: Put out as many zero pairs as the tokens that are missing, lift off the tokens being subtracted, and read the answer from the tokens that stay.
video_script.anchor: a tray of positive and negative tokens
video_script.payoff_line: The six answers are positive two, negative three, positive two, negative five, positive five and negative twelve.

final_answer.spoken: positive two, negative three, positive two, negative five, positive five and negative twelve

maths_rules: (−5) − (−7): short by 2, so 2 zero pairs; take out 7 negative tokens; 2 positive tokens stay, so +2
(+10) − (+13): short by 3, so 3 zero pairs; take out 13 positive tokens; 3 negative tokens stay, so −3
(−7) − (−9): short by 2, so 2 zero pairs; 2 positive tokens stay, so +2
(+3) − (+8): short by 5, so 5 zero pairs; 5 negative tokens stay, so −5
(−2) − (−7): short by 5, so 5 zero pairs; 5 positive tokens stay, so +5
(+3) − (+15): short by 12, so 12 zero pairs; 12 negative tokens stay, so −12

check: 2 positive and 7 negative less 2 zero pairs = 5 negative; 3 negative and 13 positive less 3 zero pairs = 10 positive; 2 positive and 9 negative less 2 zero pairs = 7 negative; 5 negative and 8 positive less 5 zero pairs = 3 positive; 5 positive and 7 negative less 5 zero pairs = 2 negative; 12 negative and 15 positive less 12 zero pairs = 3 positive
video_script.design: Six subtractions on one board. In each, the number of zero pairs equals the tokens that are missing from the tray. The check puts the taken tokens back.

narration: <bookmark mark='pair'/>One positive token and one negative token together are worth zero.
<bookmark mark='name'/>Such a pair of tokens is called a zero pair.
<bookmark mark='put'/>When the tray has too few tokens, we put out zero pairs first. They do not change the value of the tray.
